$comment: Content for Equalize (node g26, ages 12-15, Chapter 4): NEW v2 build to GDD 26 (mechanic-embodying), the
gender-equality BALANCING-SIM node (Thread E · Gender & Respect). "Equality isn't just a belief: it's
something you live, and it lifts everyone." 84 researched, India-grounded scenarios across the
belief-vs-practice → unpaid-load → pay-and-power → pays-off → child-marriage → rebalance-it arc, each
encoded as one of the shared v2 play actions (branch / strike-rewrite / sort / reflect / match / role-play /
build): no binary "tap the right card". Lead mechanics: branch (rebalance choices ×23), strike-rewrite
(bust the myth ×17), sort (gap vs lived practice ×15). Teaches: spotting the gap between believing in
equality and living it, the invisible unpaid-care load, pay & power gaps, how equality PAYS OFF for
everyone (boys/men included: it's not zero-sum), and rebalancing home/school/community. EVENHANDED.
CHILD MARRIAGE is handled as a RIGHTS ISSUE: respectful, non-graphic, legally accurate (illegal in India;
18 for girls), never blaming the target ("it's not her fault"), evenhanded (it harms boys too), and it
always routes an at-risk child to a trusted adult / Childline 1098. Builds on g10 (Fair Play World); prereq
g25. Rendered by the shared engine (components/games/v2-engine.tsx). gameId "equalize". DO NOT RENAME.

myth.why: Same work earns the same wage, whoever does it.

scenarios.relearn: Pay follows the job, not a guess about who has a family.

scenarios.hook: "Women don't apply for promotions, so it's their own fault."

myth.un: Women just don't apply, so the gap is their own doing.
myth.re: Many don't apply because the rules feel rigged; fix the rules and they do.
myth.why: Clear, open promotions bring far more women forward.

scenarios.relearn: Hidden, biased promotion rules hold women back, not a lack of trying.

scenarios.hook: "A woman has never really run anything big in India."

scenarios.relearn: Indian women have led the nation; 'never run anything big' is plainly false.

scenarios.hook: "She only got promoted to fill a quota."

myth.re: Opening a door women were kept from isn't a handout; she still earns it.
myth.why: Removing a barrier lets real talent through.

scenarios.relearn: Fair access isn't a favour; women earn the roles they're finally allowed to reach.

scenarios.hook: "To be taken seriously, a woman boss must act like a man."

myth.un: A woman has to act like a man to be respected as a boss.
myth.re: There's no one 'manly' way to lead; she can lead well as herself.
myth.why: Results, not a borrowed style, earn respect.

scenarios.relearn: Women lead as themselves; there's no single 'manly' way to be the boss.

scenarios.hook: "If a woman leads, the men under her lose respect."

myth.un: Men lose respect if they have to work under a woman.
myth.re: A good boss lifts the whole team, and the team gets the credit too.
myth.why: Strong leadership helps everyone who works with it.

scenarios.relearn: A capable woman boss lifts her team; no one loses by being led well.

scenarios.hook: "Women choose low-paying work, so the gap is fair."

myth.un: The gap is fair because women simply choose low-paying work.

myth.why: Same role, lower pay is bias, not a career pick.

scenarios.relearn: Same-job pay gaps aren't a 'choice'; that part is bias.

scenarios.hook: "Girls shouldn't aim for leadership; it'll only disappoint them."

myth.un: Girls shouldn't aim high; leadership will only let them down.
myth.re: It's barriers, not ability, that stop women; aim high and push the barriers.
myth.why: Women lead everywhere once doors open.

scenarios.relearn: Aim high; it's barriers, not lack of ability, that hold women back.

scenarios.hook: "Mentoring women is unfair to the men who miss out."

scenarios.relearn: Mentoring women balances an old head start; it isn't unfair to men.

scenarios.hook: "A woman in charge means the place will fall apart."

myth.re: Teams run on skill and planning, both of which have no gender.
myth.why: Plenty of women run large teams and whole companies well.

scenarios.relearn: Good management isn't gendered; women run teams and firms successfully.

scenarios.hook: "He talked over her, but that's just being confident."

myth.why: Letting all voices land gets the best ideas.

scenarios.relearn: Real confidence shares the floor; talking over people isn't a strength.

scenarios.hook: "Why bother? Nothing about pay and power ever changes."

myth.why: Each push closed a gap that once felt fixed.

scenarios.relearn: Pay and power gaps have shrunk before; pushing on them works.

scenarios.hook: "A dad who cooks and changes nappies looks soft."

myth.why: Being close to your children is strength, not softness.

scenarios.relearn: A hands-on dad gains a closer family; that's the payoff.

myth.un: After her job, the housework is just hers to finish.
myth.re: When both work outside, the home shift is shared too.
myth.why: Paid work then all the chores is a double day; sharing it is true equality.

scenarios.relearn: The home shift is shared when both partners work outside too.

scenarios.hook: Flip the myth about men and the kitchen.

myth.un: Men just can't cook or run a kitchen.
myth.re: Anyone can learn to cook and run a kitchen with a little practice.
myth.why: Cooking is a skill picked up by doing, not a talent handed to one gender.

scenarios.relearn: Cooking is a learnable skill, not a gift reserved for women.

scenarios.hook: Flip the myth about leaving your own mess.

myth.un: Cleaning up after me is just her thing.
myth.re: Owning your own mess is everyone's basic share of the home.
myth.why: Leaving your dishes 'because that's her job' just loads someone else.

scenarios.relearn: Carrying your own mess is basic fairness, not someone else's job.

scenarios.hook: Say it: propose sharing the home load, warmly, not as an attack.
scenarios.setup: You want your family to split the chores more fairly. How do you open it?

yourLine.text: Mum does so much alone. Could we make a rota and all take a share?
It's not my problem if the housework's unfair.

scenarios.relearn: You can warmly propose fairer sharing at home, not as an attack.

scenarios.hook: Say it: your sister's stuck cooking while you're free.
scenarios.setup: She's revising over the stove again. What do you say?

yourLine.text: You study. I've got the cooking tonight, swap me back another day.
That's your job, not mine.

scenarios.relearn: Offering to swap chores frees a girl's study time, not just yours.

scenarios.hook: Say it: a relative tells only the girls to go serve.
scenarios.setup: Aunty says 'girls, go serve the guests'. You want to share it. What do you say?

yourLine.text: I'll take a serving round too. Let's not leave it all to them.
Yeah, girls, off you go.

scenarios.relearn: Offering to serve too shares hosting beyond just the girls.

scenarios.hook: Say it: back your dad when he's teased for doing laundry.
scenarios.setup: A neighbour mocks your dad for 'women's work'. What do you say?

yourLine.text: He's just sharing the home. That's exactly how it should be.
Nothing: let the teasing slide.

scenarios.relearn: Backing a man who shares chores keeps it normal, not 'weak'.

scenarios.hook: Say it: own up when you've been skipping your chore turns.
scenarios.setup: Asha's been covering the rota turns you 'forgot'. What do you say?

yourLine.text: I've been dumping my turns on you. That stops now, I'll do mine.
You don't really mind covering, right?

scenarios.relearn: Owning your skipped turns stops quietly dumping them on someone.

scenarios.hook: Say it: offer to take a whole task off Mum's mental load.
scenarios.setup: Mum tracks every bill, birthday and refill alone. What do you say?

yourLine.text: Let me fully own the groceries. One less list running in your head.
Just tell me if you ever need a hand.

scenarios.relearn: Owning a whole task lifts the planning, not just 'helping' when asked.

scenarios.hook: Say it: a friend brags he's never washed a plate.
scenarios.setup: He calls never cleaning 'a man thing'. What do you say?

yourLine.text: Never cleaning isn't a flex. It just means someone else carries you.
Haha, lucky you, plates aren't our problem.

scenarios.relearn: Never doing chores isn't pride; it just loads someone else.

scenarios.hook: Say it: gently name the gap in a 'we're equal' home.
scenarios.setup: Your uncle insists the home's totally equal, but only aunty cooks and cleans. What do you say?

yourLine.text: We say it's equal, but the work's all on aunty. Shall we share it?
Sure, uncle, sounds equal to me.

scenarios.relearn: Naming the gap kindly is how you turn 'we're equal' into reality.
